items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed; high release risk. Fleet-wide clearance is unsupported because fleet-doctor has no run, findings, or checks, while operations has no deploy, uptime, or error-sweep results. Authentication/access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS enforcement, data exposure, monitoring/incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unevidenced. Recommendation: keep security-sensitive releases and gated public exposure blocked; permit ordinary reversible growth only when it adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Do not claim certification or a clean bill of health.

Continue the existing canonical fleet security evidence matrix without creating duplicate work. Use authorized metadata and retained artifacts only to document dated evidence, affected scope, owners, severity, and release implications for access boundaries, secrets, isolation, release/deploy controls, dependencies, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, and disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions/configuration, add dependencies, or deploy.

SearchWoot remains private from a security perspective: security and related launch evidence are incomplete. No incident, breach, secret exposure, authentication failure, dependency compromise, or isolation failure is established; these remain unknown because telemetry is absent. The compliance baseline is technical only: 35 pass, 20 fail, and 6 unknown across 61 sites. No TLS certificates are reported as expiring within 30 days, but TLS configuration and enforcement are not evidenced.
